subject: Defect review of src/billing/ — blind commit, then cross-attack
shape: Blind commit, then cross-attack (+ fresh-eyes verdict)
termination: Ended at round cap — 2 points unresolved
bindingAnchor: Pinned to commit range a3f19c2..7e44b81 · joint list recorded against src/billing/ at 7e44b81

findings.text: invoice.py:41 — invoice_total accumulates currency in float; rounding at the end hides per-line drift.
webhooks.py:88 — the payment.settled handler has no idempotency check; a redelivered webhook credits the account twice.
charge.py:57 — the retry loop backs off exponentially but without jitter; synchronized retries can stampede the payment gateway.
No idempotency check on payment.settled webhooks.
Retry backoff lacks jitter in charge.py.
credits.py:19 — apply_credit does an unlocked read-modify-write of account.balance; concurrent credits race.
periods.py:33 — period_end is compared as a timezone-naive datetime; billing day boundaries shift with the server locale.
refunds.py:62 — the refund path swallows GatewayError and marks the invoice refunded anyway.

blindCommit.overlapNote: Overlap between the two blind lists: 0 of 6 findings — each reading covered blind spots the other missed, which is why this shape exists.

objection.title: Float drift changes charged totals
objection.reason: Reproduced: 34-line invoice totals one cent high; Decimal fix agreed.

content.text: Your C1 understates the defect. The drift is not merely cosmetic — it changes the total customers are charged:

With 30+ metered lines the accumulated error crosses a cent boundary, so round() settles on the wrong side. This must be fixed with Decimal end to end in the totaling path, not patched with per-line rounding.

Accepted. Reproduced with a 34-line metered invoice: the float total lands one cent high. The fix converts invoice_total and its helpers to Decimal with cent quantization; C1 is upgraded from style concern to charging defect and merged with this objection in the joint list.

objection.title: Webhook redelivery double-credits
objection.reason: Gap conceded; unique-constraint dedupe on gateway event id agreed.

content.text: On your C2: what exactly happens today when the gateway redelivers a payment.settled event — and where would your proposed dedupe record live so that two concurrent deliveries cannot both pass the check?

Today both deliveries credit the account; nothing dedupes. The gap the question exposes is real: a check-then-insert dedupe still races. Conceded and folded into the joint list — the fix stores the gateway event id in a processed_events table with a unique constraint, and treats the constraint violation as “already handled”.

objection.title: Decimal migration must reach the schema
objection.reason: Column already stores integer cents; no float read path shown.

content.text: The Decimal migration agreed in round 1 is incomplete unless it extends to persistence: the invoices.total column must move to a fixed-point type in the same change, otherwise you reintroduce float on every read.

Rejected. The column already stores integer cents (BIGINT, see schema.sql:112); floats exist only in the in-memory totaling path that round 1 fixes. A schema migration would be churn without a defect behind it. Rebuttal stands unless Codex can show a read path that materializes the column as float — it did not.

objection.title: Timezone-naive period_end
objection.reason: Defect real, but anchor timezone is a product decision; cap ended debate.

content.text: My X2 stands and your joint list still omits it: period_end comparisons are timezone-naive, so the billing day boundary moves when the host timezone changes. Pinning to UTC is a one-line fix and should go in now.

The defect is real, but “pin to UTC” is not obviously the fix: invoices are contractually cut at midnight in the customer’s billing timezone, and UTC pinning would shift existing customers’ period boundaries. Choosing the anchor timezone is a product decision, not a code ruling. Left unresolved — the round cap ended the debate here; the point is recorded for the owner to decide.

agreed.text: Joint defect list covers C1+#1 (Decimal totaling), C2+#2 (webhook dedupe via unique constraint), C3 (retry jitter), X1 (credit race — row lock on account.balance), and X3 (refund path must not swallow GatewayError).
The invoices.total column stays BIGINT integer cents; no schema migration (objection #3 rejected).
The joint list is recorded against src/billing/ at commit 7e44b81, per the binding anchor.

unresolved.text: Objection #4 — timezone anchor for period_end. Escalated to the owner.
unresolved.attribution: Codex holds UTC pinning should land now; Claude holds the anchor timezone is a product decision.

unresolved.text: Fresh-eyes finding F2 — multi-currency accounts were outside the reviewed scope; expanding scope needs an owner decision.

devilsAdvocate.title: Devil’s-advocate verdict
devilsAdvocate.intro: Codex prosecuted the decision to keep webhook processing synchronous; Claude defended it. The decision survives on its merits, with the obligations the prosecution earned:

points.label: Residual risk
points.text: a gateway retry storm can saturate the worker pool; mitigation is the per-endpoint rate limit agreed in round 1.

points.label: Residual risk
points.text: synchronous processing couples webhook latency to database write latency; revisit if p99 exceeds the gateway’s 10-second delivery timeout.

points.label: Obligation
points.text: the rejected async alternative is re-tabled automatically if either risk materializes.

objection.title: Dedupe table grows unbounded
objection.reason: Agreed fix stored event ids forever; 90-day TTL added.

content.text: The agreed webhook dedupe stores every gateway event id in processed_events with no expiry. At current volume that table grows by ~2M rows/month forever; the unique-constraint lookup degrades with it. The agreement shipped a slow leak.

Accepted. A compromise blind spot: both debaters focused on correctness of the dedupe and neither priced its growth. The joint list gains a 90-day TTL purge (the gateway redelivers for at most 72 hours, so 90 days is conservative).

objection.title: Multi-currency accounts uncovered
objection.reason: Out of the reviewed scope; needs an owner decision on whether to expand it.

content.text: The entire joint list assumes single-currency accounts, but credits.py accepts a currency argument it never validates against the account’s ledger currency. A EUR credit applied to a USD account passes silently.

Unresolved. The observation is plausible, but multi-currency behavior was outside the reviewed scope pinned at a3f19c2..7e44b81, and validating it means expanding the review. Recorded as open for the owner rather than folded into the agreement — the binding record covers only what was reviewed.
